findings.title: Federated rule group detection removed from ruler abilities, allowing edit/delete of federated rules
findings.body: In useAllRulerRuleAbilities, the previous implementation computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` from the CombinedRule's group, and treated federated rules as immutable (`immutableRule = isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided`), which prevented Update/Delete/Pause/Duplicate on federated rule groups. The new implementation hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO comment. Since useAllRulerRuleAbilities now only receives a RulerRuleDTO and a groupIdentifier (which contains no source_tenants information), federated Mimir rule groups will no longer be detected as immutable. This means users may be shown Edit/Delete/Pause/Duplicate actions for federated rules that cannot actually be modified through the ruler API, and clicking them will produce failed API calls or, worse, the UI will incorrectly report the user as permitted to modify rules they cannot. The ability check no longer matches the server-side enforcement for federated groups.

findings.title: Update/Delete abilities for ruler rules no longer check ruler availability correctly when rule is undefined
findings.body: In useAllRulerRuleAbilities, `MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : isRulerAvailable`. When the list view no longer fetches ruler rules, `rule` is undefined and `useIsRuleEditable(rulesSourceName, undefined)` is called. The behavior of useIsRuleEditable with an undefined rule is not shown, but if it returns isRulerAvailable=true (e.g., based on data source features rather than an actual ruler rule), then for cloud (data source) rules in contexts where AlertRuleMenu still calls useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule=undefined, ...), the Update/Delete abilities could incorrectly report supported=true. Combined with the OR logic in AlertRuleMenu (`canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`), a false positive from the ruler path could enable actions. The ruler ability path should return NotSupported when rule is undefined, but the current code relies on useIsRuleEditable's behavior with undefined input which is not guaranteed to be conservative.

This means when a user navigates from the rule list to a rule's view page and then back, they will not return to the list view with the same scroll position/filter state — they will land on the default view. This is a UX regression: the back navigation behavior is broken compared to the old implementation.

findings.title: Redundant type check in alerting rule branch
findings.body: `const promAlertingRule = rule && rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting ? rule : undefined;` — this check is redundant because the enclosing `if (prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule))` already guarantees that `rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting` (isGrafanaPromAlertingRule checks `isAlertingRule(rule)` which checks `rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting`). The `rule &&` part is also unnecessary since rule is a required prop. This is dead code that could confuse readers, though it doesn't cause a bug.

findings.title: Creating/Deleting rule states are no longer shown because ruler data is not fetched
findings.body: The old GrafanaGroupLoader fetched both Prometheus groups and Ruler groups, matched them, and displayed 'Creating' state for ruler rules without a Prometheus counterpart, and 'Deleting' state for Prometheus rules without a Ruler counterpart (via RuleOperationListItem). The new implementation only fetches Prometheus groups (`useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery`) and renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules`. Rules that are being created (exist in ruler but not yet in Prometheus) or being deleted (exist in Prometheus but removed from ruler) will no longer be shown in the list at all. This is a functional regression: users will not see rules in transitional Creating/Deleting states, which was an intentional UX feature. The tests for these states were removed (the old tests 'should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists' and 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists' were deleted).

findings.title: Missing key prop on GrafanaRuleListItem in FilterView usage
findings.body: In FilterView.tsx line 157, `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} namespaceName={ruleWithOrigin.namespaceName} showLocation={true} />` is rendered without a `key` prop. The surrounding `rules.map()` uses `key` for other branches (DataSourceRuleLoader gets `key={key}`, UnknownRuleListItem gets `key={key}`), but the GrafanaRuleListItem branch is missing the key. React will warn about missing keys in lists, and reconciliation may be inefficient. The `key` variable is available in scope (destructured from ruleWithOrigin at line 152) and should be passed as `key={key}`.

findings.title: Extra closing brace in Grafana rule key template literal
findings.body: `return `grafana-${namespace.uid}-${groupName}-${rule.uid}}`;` — there is an extra `}` at the end of the template literal before the closing backtick. This produces keys like `grafana-uid-groupname-ruleuid}` with a trailing `}`. While this doesn't break uniqueness (the extra character is consistent), it's clearly a typo and produces malformed keys. It should be `grafana-${namespace.uid}-${groupName}-${rule.uid}`.

findings.title: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities calls useFolder for every rule, causing N+1 folder fetches in list view
findings.body: `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` calls `useFolder(folderUID)` for each rule. In the alert list view with ~80 rules, this means up to 80 calls to useFolder. If useFolder fetches folder data via API (not cached), this results in N+1 requests. The old implementation used `useIsRuleEditable(rulesSourceName, rule)` which likely had similar behavior, but the new hook is called from AlertRuleMenu and RuleActionsButtons for every rule in the list. If folders are cached by RTK Query, this is fine, but if not, this is a significant performance regression. The comment in the old code ('This hook is being called a lot in different places... In some cases multiple times for ~80 rules') suggests this was a known concern. Additionally, `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport` calls `useGetGrafanaAlertingConfigurationStatusQuery` for every rule — this is an RTK Query hook so it should be cached/deduplicated, but worth verifying.

findings.title: skipToken pattern violates Rules of Hooks — useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is always called even when skipToken is passed
findings.body: The `skipToken` pattern is used to conditionally skip the `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` hooks when the rule is not a Grafana prom rule. However, looking at the implementation: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(rule, action)` calls `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(rule === skipToken ? undefined : rule)` unconditionally. This means `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` is ALWAYS called, which internally calls `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(undefined)`, `useAlertingAbility`, `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport`, and `useCanSilenceInFolder(undefined)`. These hooks are always executed regardless of skipToken. The skipToken only affects the `rule` parameter passed to useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities (undefined vs actual rule), not whether the hooks run. This is actually fine for Rules of Hooks (hooks are always called in the same order), but the skipToken pattern is misleading — it doesn't actually skip any hook execution, it just passes undefined. The real concern is that `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(undefined)` calls `useFolder(undefined)` and `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()` calls an API query — these run for EVERY rule in the list, including cloud rules where they're irrelevant. For cloud rules, this means unnecessary folder lookups and potentially unnecessary API calls.

findings.title: Test names are inverted — 'Should not render Edit button for users with the update permission' tests the wrong scenario
findings.body: The test at line 63 is named 'Should not render Edit button for users with the update permission' but it mocks `useIsRuleEditable.mockReturnValue({ loading: false, isEditable: true })` — i.e., the user HAS the update permission (isEditable: true). The assertion is `expect(ui.actionButtons.edit.query()).not.toBeInTheDocument()` — expecting the Edit button NOT to be rendered. This is contradictory: if the user has update permission (isEditable: true), the Edit button SHOULD be rendered. Either the test name is wrong (should be 'without the update permission') or the mock/assertion is wrong. The same issue exists at lines 74, 89, and 100. These tests are either testing the wrong thing or have inverted names, making them unreliable as regression tests.

findings.title: Test mocks useGrafanaPromRuleAbility but the component uses useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities (plural)
findings.body: In the 'Grafana rules action buttons' tests, `mocks.useGrafanaPromRuleAbility.mockImplementation(...)` is set up (singular hook), but the AlertRuleMenu component uses `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (plural). The test also mocks `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` separately. The singular hook mock is unnecessary for these tests since RuleActionsButtons.V2 uses `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` (singular) for the Edit button check, but the test setup is confusing — it mocks both singular and plural hooks with similar logic. If RuleActionsButtons.V2 is the component under test, the singular mock is relevant; if AlertRuleMenu is also rendered (via the More button), the plural mock is relevant. The test setup is overly complex and potentially fragile, but not necessarily wrong.

findings.title: Test asserts exactly 4 menu items but Delete is missing from the expected list despite delete permissions being granted
findings.body: The test 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' grants delete permissions (`AccessControlAction.AlertingRuleDelete` in both grantUserPermissions and setFolderAccessControl) and asserts `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` with expected items: Silence, Copy link, Duplicate, Export. However, Delete is NOT in the expected list despite delete permissions being granted. Looking at AlertRuleMenu, the Delete menu item requires `canDelete && rulerRule` — since rulerRule is undefined in the list view (per the PR's goal of removing ruler API calls), the Delete item will not render. So the test passes with 4 items, but this actually documents the bug: Delete is silently missing from the menu even when the user has delete permission. The test should either expect Delete to be present (and fail, revealing the bug) or explicitly document that Delete is not available in the list view. As written, the test masks the regression.

findings.title: Test 'should not render edit button when user lacks edit permissions' doesn't revoke global permissions
findings.body: The test overrides folder access control to deny editing (`setFolderAccessControl({ [AccessControlAction.AlertingRuleUpdate]: false, ... })`), but the `beforeEach` grants global permissions via `grantUserPermissions([AccessControlAction.AlertingRuleUpdate, ...])`. The `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` hook checks `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(rulesPermissions.update, folder)` — this checks folder-scoped permissions in metadata, not global permissions. However, if the permission check falls back to global permissions when folder metadata doesn't have the permission, the test might not actually deny edit access. The test asserts the edit button is not present, but if the global permission grants edit access regardless of folder metadata, the test would fail — or if it passes, it might be because the folder metadata check correctly overrides. This is unclear from the code shown and the test may not be testing what it claims.

findings.title: Stale comment about ruler preload after removing ruler prefetch
findings.body: The comment at lines 81-82 says 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX / Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded'. However, the ruler prefetch code (`alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)`) was removed in this PR. The comment now refers to preloading ruler rules that are no longer being preloaded. The comment should be updated to reflect that only Prometheus groups are cached now, or removed entirely.

findings.title: Misleading comment '// duplicate' on useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable call
findings.body: Line 289 has the comment `// duplicate` after `const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate`. This comment is unclear — it might mean the hook is a duplicate of useIsRuleEditable, or that the call is duplicated. It should be clarified or removed.

findings.title: UnknownRuleListItem missing key prop when used as fallback
findings.body: The fallback `return <UnknownRuleListItem ruleName={name} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} ruleDefinition={rule} />;` at line 70 doesn't include a `key` prop. While this is the return value of a component (not directly in a list), if GrafanaRuleListItem is rendered in a list (which it is, in GrafanaGroupLoader and FilterView), the parent should provide the key. The parent components do provide keys (GrafanaGroupLoader uses `key={promRule.uid}`, FilterView should use `key={key}` but doesn't — see separate finding). This is not a bug in this file per se, but the component doesn't enforce or document key requirements.

findings.title: copyToClipboard doesn't handle clipboard write failure
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard?.writeText(text).then(() => { appEvents.emit(AppEvents.alertSuccess, ['URL copied to clipboard']); });` — there is no `.catch()` handler. If the clipboard write fails (e.g., permission denied, document not focused), the promise rejects and an unhandled promise rejection occurs. The user gets no feedback that the copy failed. A `.catch()` should be added to show an error message.
